analysis: This batch contains documentation only: a new changelog (changelog.d/ssd-retirement-in-slices.md lines 1-9) and docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md. In the reference, line 3 changes the date and head line 377 describes owned retirement running SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.filesPerSlice = 16 files per hold of the removal lock and epoch barrier (removeInSlices). The doc says each hold rechecks ownership and a refusal ends the batch. Relevant model entries: T-041 TTL/LRU sweep bounds the reuse window, and the epoch is a routing generation, not a purge primitive. Security implications to verify in source (SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.swift, SSDCacheEpochStore.performOwnedRetirement, SSDDiskBudget.retireActiveEntries), which was not supplied here: (1) A refusal or disown mid-batch now leaves the remaining TTL-expired files undeleted until the next sweep. Confirm that readers still refuse expired entries by TTL at lookup. Otherwise the 30-minute T-041/SEC-035 reuse bound could stretch to roughly a sweep interval (60 s) or longer. (2) Lookups and donor index publication that interleave between slices must not resurrect or re-index a victim. They must not publish ready evidence for a file about to be unlinked; the cache_entry_evicted path should cover this. (3) The per-file lease try-without-wait and the skip of renamed-but-unindexed files must remain correct for each slice. (4) Ownership recheck per slice must use the same no-follow epoch-record read semantics (base line 378). No regression is established from the docs. The change narrows lock-hold latency, an availability improvement, and does not alter crypto, naming, TTL constants or scope binding. Implementation review is needed to confirm the TTL enforcement claim.
